title: Complainants Filed A Complaint v. Potomac Presbytery
disposition_detail: Issue 1 (whether Potomac Presbytery erred in its 11/12/91 adjudication): complaint not sustained. Complaints #2 and #3: dismissed as not timely filed (Panel had found them 'not judicially in order' on 2/28/92; SJC ratified the dismissal on 3/7/92). The timely 12/11/91 complaint (#1) was heard 3/6/92. Judgment and Disposition approved 21-0, 1 disqualified.
first_summary: Complainants challenged Potomac Presbytery's handling of the Timonium Presbyterian Church pastoral dispute, arguing the Presbytery gave too little time and explanation before denying their complaint. The SJC affirmed Presbytery, holding that a higher court may not overturn a competent lower court merely because complainants are dissatisfied with the deliberation or input given. Two related complaints were dismissed as untimely. Complaint not sustained.
summary: Complainants challenged Potomac Presbytery's 11/12/91 adjudication denying their complaint over the Timonium Presbyterian Church pastoral dispute, arguing they received too little time, deliberation, and explanation. The SJC held the complaint not sustained: a higher court may not overturn a competent lower court merely because complainants are dissatisfied with the amount of input or time spent, and no constitutional defect was demonstrated. Two earlier complaints were dismissed as not timely filed. The timely 12/11/91 complaint was heard 3/6/92.
